problem: Which of the following functions is continuous on the interval $[1,4]?$
worked_solution:
The correct answer is the following. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13945275/assets/03d8fa6c421deebb49b3746425f799a2eea7fc22f07175bb1cf80d270f896555.png)

  

Indeed, this function is continuous on the open intervals $(-\infty ,1)$ and $(1,5).$

Additionally, the function is right-continuous at $x=1.$ Hence, it is continuous on the interval $[1,5).$

So, we can say that the function is continuous on the intervals $(-\infty ,1)$ and $[1,5).$ It is also continuous on any subinterval of these intervals.

Therefore, this function is continuous on $[1,4]$ because $[1,4]$ is contained inside the interval $[1,5).$

Notice that

- $q(x)$ is not right-continuous at $x=1,$ so it is not continuous on the interval $[1,4].$

- $f(x)$ is not defined at $x=2,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[1,4].$

- $g(x)$ has a removable discontinuity at $x=3.$ So it is not continuous on the interval $[1,4].$

- $p(x)$ is not defined at $x=4,$ and so it is not continuous on the interval $[1,4].$
